The `gridcalc` package in /app evaluates spreadsheet-style sheets of cells and formulas into JSON documents, and it has bugs. Some of its unit tests fail. From /app, run them with:

    python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .

Fix the package code under /app/gridcalc so that it follows the rules in /app/docs (start with /app/docs/overview.md). Those rules are not the ones of any spreadsheet program you may know; where they differ, the docs decide. Passing the unit tests is not enough: the package will also be run on other sheets, and every document it writes must follow the docs. Do not change anything under /app/tests, /app/data or /app/docs.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;
"summary": one or two sentences describing what you did and anything left unfinished.

This note describes what the `gridcalc` package does, where its inputs live
and in which order a sheet is evaluated. The rules for each step live in
their own notes:

| Note | Covers |
|---|---|
| `sheets.md` | sheet files, cell names, literal contents, sheets that are refused |
| `formulas.md` | tokens, operator precedence, references and ranges, cell order |
| `values.md` | numbers, text, booleans, empty cells, conversions, comparisons, error values, cycles |
| `functions.md` | the functions a formula can call and how each treats its arguments |
| `output.md` | evaluated documents, the summa

This note covers the text format of `DATA/sheets/<id>.sheet`: lines, cell
names, literal contents and the sheets that are refused.

## 1. Lines

1.1 A sheet file is read line by line. Leading and trailing spaces and tabs of
a line are ignored.

1.2 A line that is empty after that is skipped. A line whose first character
is `#` is a comment and is skipped.

1.3 Every other line defines one cell:

    CELL: CONTENT

`CELL` is a cell name (section 2). Spaces or tabs may stand between the name
and the colon. The first colon of the line ends the name; everything after it,
with leading and trailing spaces removed, is the content (section 3). A colon
inside the content, as in a range `A1:B3`, is part of the content.

1.4 The order of the lines does not matter. A formula may name a cell that is
defined further down the file.

## 2. Cell names

2.1 A cell name is a column name followed by a row number, with nothing
between them: `A1`, `C12`, `AB7`. Column and row are those of `formulas.md`
section 4. Letters may be written in either case; `ab7` is the cell `AB7`.

2.2 A sheet file names a cell without `$` signs. `$A$1` is not a cell name
here (it is a valid reference inside a formula).

2.3 The row number may have leading zeros; `A07` is the cell `A7`.

## 3. Contents

3.1 A content that starts with `=` is a formula. The whole content, including
the `=`, is the formula text. The text after `=` is read by `formulas.md`.

3.2 Any other content is a literal. It is read in this order:

1. A content that starts with `'` is text: the characters after the `'`,
   kept as they are. `'42` is the text `42`, not a number; `'TRUE` is the
   text `TRUE`.
2. A content that is a number as `values.md` 2.3 defines it is that number:
   `12`, `-4`, `0.25`, `.5`, `1.5e3`, `2E-2`.
3. `TRUE` and `FALSE`, in any case, are booleans.
4. Anything else is text, as written: `apple`, `Birch 2`, `#DIV/0!`.

3.3 A literal is never evaluated. The content `1+1` is the text `1+1`.

## 4. What a sheet defines

4.1 The cells a sheet defines are exactly the cells its lines name. Every
other cell of the grid is undefined and reads as empty (`values.md` 2.5).

4.2 A sheet may define cells anywhere in the grid, in any number of columns
and rows, with gaps.

## 5. Refused sheets

5.1 A sheet is refused, as a whole, when its file:

- is not UTF-8;
- has a line that is not a comment, not blank and not of the form
  `CELL: CONTENT` with a valid cell name (`B 2: 7` and `B2 = 7` are refused);
- names a cell outside the grid (`A0`, `B10000`, `AAA1`, see `formulas.md`
  4.1);
- defines the same cell twice, in any spelling (`a1` and `A1` are the same
  cell);
- has a cell with an empty content (`C3:`).

5.2 A refused sheet gets no document. It is listed in `errors.json` with the
error class `SheetError` (`output.md` section 4).

5.3 A formula that cannot be read is not a reason to refuse a sheet. Its cell
takes the value `#PARSE!` (`formulas.md` 2.6).

parentheses.

1.2 Spaces and tabs between tokens are ignored. They are never needed, except
inside strings, where they are kept.

This note covers the kinds of values, how one kind is read as another, how
values compare, the error values and how they spread, and cycles.

## 1. Kinds

1.1 A value is a number, a text, a boolean, empty, or an error value.

1.2 Numbers are double-precision floating point numbers. There is one kind of
number; `2` and `2.0` are the same value.

1.3 A boolean is `TRUE` or `FALSE`. A boolean is not a number, even though
it can be read as one (section 2).

1.4 Empty is the value of a cell the sheet does not define. It is neither 0
nor the text `""`; how it reads depends on where it is used (2.5, 4.2,
`functions.md`).

## 2. Reading one kind as another

2.1 **As a number** (operands of `+ - * / ^`, prefix `-` and `+`, `%`, and
the arguments `functions.md` says are read as numbers): a number is itself;
`TRUE` is 1 and `FALSE` is 0; empty is 0; a text that holds a number
(2.3) is that number; any other text gives `#VALUE!`.

2.2 **As text** (operands of `&`, and the arguments `functions.md` says are
read as text): a text is itself; a number is written as in section 3;
`TRUE` and `FALSE` are the texts `TRUE` and `FALSE`; empty is the text `""`.

2.3 A text holds a number when, after leading and trailing spaces and tabs
are removed, it is an optional sign followed by a number written as in
`formulas.md` 2.1: `"42"`, `" -1.5 "`, `"1e3"` and `".5"` hold numbers;
`"1,000"`, `"5%"`, `"0x1F"` and `""` do not.

2.4 **As a boolean** (the condition of `IF`, the arguments of `AND`, `OR`
and `NOT`): a boolean is itself; a number is `TRUE` unless it is 0; empty is
`FALSE`; the texts `TRUE` and `FALSE`, in any case, are those booleans; any
other text gives `#VALUE!`.

2.5 **Empty.** An undefined cell read by an operator is converted by 2.1,
2.2 or 2.4 like any other value: `A9+1` is 1 and `A9&"x"` is `x` when `A9` is
undefined. Functions treat empty cells on their own terms (`functions.md`
1.2). A formula whose result is empty, such as `=A9`, has the value 0.

## 3. Numbers as text

3.1 A number becomes text when `&`, `CONCAT` or `LEN` read it as text.

3.2 The text of a number is its `%.10g` form, as C's `printf` writes it: at
most 10 significant digits, without trailing zeros and without a trailing
decimal point. The exponent form is used when the decimal exponent is below
-4 or at least 10, with a sign and at least two digits. Negative zero is
written `0`.

| Number | Text |
|---|---|
| 2 | `2` |
| 0.5 | `0.5` |
| 1/3 | `0.3333333333` |
| 0.1+0.2 | `0.3` |
| 1234567.125 | `1234567.125` |
| 12345678901 | `1.23456789e+10` |
| 0.000012 | `1.2e-05` |

## 4. Comparisons

4.1 The comparison operators give `TRUE` or `FALSE`. An operand that is an
error value gives that error instead (section 5).

4.2 When one operand is empty, it is read as the blank of the other one's
kind: 0 next to a number, `""` next to a text, `FALSE` next to a boolean.
Two empty operands are equal. So with `A9` undefined, `A9=0`, `A9=""` and
`A9=FALSE` are all `TRUE`.

4.3 Values of the same kind compare naturally: numbers by size, booleans with
`FALSE` before `TRUE`, and texts by code point order after both are put in
lower case, so `"apple"="APPLE"` is `TRUE` and `"a"<"B"` is `TRUE`.

4.4 Values of different kinds are never equal and order as numbers before

`1="1"` is `FALSE`. A text is not read as a number for a comparison.

import re
from dataclasses import dataclass

from .errors import FormulaError

NUMBER = r"(?:[0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]*)?|\.[0-9]+)"
# Longer operators first, so that '<=' is not read as '<' followed by '='.
OPERATORS = ("<>", "<=", ">=", "+", "-", "*", "/", "^", "&", "=", "<", ">", "%", "(", ")", ",", ":")

_NUMBER = re.compile(NUMBER)
_REF = re.compile(r"\$?[A-Za-z]+\$?[0-9]+(?![A-Za-z0-9_(])")
_NAME = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Token:
    kind: str  # num, str, ref, name or op
    text: str


def _string(text: str, i: int) -> tuple[str, int]:
    """The value of the string literal that opens at text[i], and the index after it."""
    buf, j = [], i + 1
    while True:
        if j >= len(text):
            raise FormulaError("unterminated string")
        if text[j] == '"':
            if text[j + 1:j + 2] == '"':
                buf.append('"')
                j += 2
                continue
            return "".join(buf), j + 1
        buf.append(text[j])
        j += 1


def tokenize(text: str) -> list[Token]:
    out, i = [], 0
    while i < len(text):
        c = text[i]
        if c in " \t":
            i += 1
            continue
        if c == '"':
            value, i = _string(text, i)
            out.append(Token("str", value))
            continue
        if c.isdigit() or c == ".":
            m = _NUMBER.match(text, i)
            if not m:
                raise FormulaError(f"bad number at {i + 1}")
            out.append(Token("num", m.group()))
            i = m.end()
            continue
        m = _REF.match(text, i) or _NAME.match(text, i)
        if m:
            out.append(Token("ref" if m.re is _REF else "name", m.group()))
            i = m.end()
            continue
        for op in OPERATORS:
            if text.startswith(op, i):
                out.append(Token("op", op))
                i += len(op)
                break
        else:
            raise FormulaError(f"unexpected character {c!r} at {i + 1}")
    return out

I fixed the bugs in `/app/gridcalc`, and all 58 unit tests now pass (`python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`). `tools/check.py` is clean on all 114 evaluated sheets. It only checks structural properties of the documents, though, so I also tried about 90 edge cases from the docs by hand. Two of my own expectations didn't match: `SUM("x",1/0)` gives `#DIV/0!`, which is what the docs say, and my test value for `2^0.5%` was a placeholder. I also ran odd sheets through `run`, `show` and `cell`: duplicate cells, an empty content, invalid UTF-8, `A0`, cycles and reversed ranges.

What I fixed:

- **Columns and tokens:**
  - `col_index` now numbers columns correctly (`ZZ` is 702, so `AAA1` is outside the grid).
  - Number tokens and numeric text accept exponents such as `1e3`.
- **Precedence:**
  - Prefix minus is now looser than `^`, so `-2^2` is -4.
  - `^` groups to the right, so `2^3^2` is 512.
- **Values and numbers as text:**
  - Number text uses the `%.10g` form.
  - An undefined cell now reads as empty rather than 0.
- **Ranges and refs listings:**
  - Ranges work from any corner.
  - Refs listings have no repeats.
- **Document output:**
  - Cells are written in cell order, so `A9` comes before `A10`.
  - Booleans are typed `bool`, not `number`.
- **Functions:**
  - `IF` only evaluates the branch it takes.
  - Text that holds a number is skipped inside the references given to `SUM`, `AVERAGE`, `MIN` and `MAX`.
  - Overflowing sums give `#NUM!` instead of crashing.
  - `ROUND` no longer crashes on very large numbers.
- **Sheet files:** lines are trimmed of spaces and tabs only, as `sheets.md` says.

One change goes beyond the docs. I replaced `math.fsum` with a plain `sum` in `SUM` and `AVERAGE`. The docs say only "adds the numbers", and `fsum` raised `OverflowError` on overflow. Results can differ in the last bits, which the 10-significant-digit rounding normally hides.
